text: A bellwether is something whose behaviour is an early sign of what will happen more widely; the word comes from the lead sheep that wore a bell so the flock would follow. Minas Gerais is Brazil's bellwether state because its voters tend to tell you how the whole country will go.
To annul something is to declare it officially invalid, as if it never happened. Mr Bolsonaro says he will try to get the whole election result thrown out after losing.
Lavish means given or spent in very generous, even extravagant amounts. Brazilian leaders often hand out big benefits before an election, and Lula was generous even by that standard.

A run-off is a second election between the top two finishers when nobody wins more than half the votes in the first round. It is a fresh contest, which is how Lula could trail in round one and still win.
A comeback is a return to success after a period of failure or decline. Lula looked beaten after the first round and then won.
Pundits are commentators who are regarded as experts and give opinions on politics or other topics in the media. Most of them thought Lula was finished.
If something is dead and buried, it is completely finished and no one expects it to return. Here it means Lula's campaign was thought to be over.
Hard-right describes politics at the far, uncompromising end of the right wing. Jair Bolsonaro is described this way.
House arrest is a punishment or restriction in which a person must stay at home instead of being in prison. Jair Bolsonaro is under it for trying to stay in power by force.
A coup is a sudden, illegal seizure of power from a government, often by the military or other powerful people. Jair Bolsonaro faces consequences for attempting one.
Spoiled here has a voting meaning: a spoiled ballot is one that is filled in wrongly or marked on purpose so that it does not count. Many such voters switched to Lula in the second round.
A tactical overhaul is a complete rethinking of how a campaign is run, such as its methods and messages, rather than its goals. Lula changed from old-fashioned to online methods.
Analogue means old-fashioned and not digital. Lula's early campaign relied on stickers and rallies instead of online content.
Mojo is informal slang for a magic quality of confidence and appeal. Saying Lula discovered his mojo means he found his energy again.
A technophobe is someone who dislikes or fears modern technology. It is a surprise that Lula, once a technophobe, ended up winning online.
To go viral is to spread very quickly and widely across the internet as people share it. Lula's image did this thanks to the "missions" given to supporters.
Minas Gerais is a large, populous state in southeastern Brazil, often seen as a mirror of the country as a whole.
Evangelical refers to a branch of Protestant Christianity that stresses personal faith and spreading its message. It is a large political force in Brazil.
A spigot is a tap. Saying the government opened the spigots is a metaphor for it suddenly letting money flow out in handouts.
Handouts are money or goods given freely, often by a government to people who need them. Here they are payments from Brazil's welfare programme.
A flagship is the most important or best-known item in a group, like the lead ship of a fleet. Here it is the main welfare programme.
An incumbent is someone who currently holds an office, such as a sitting president. Incumbents often try to please voters before elections.
A sole trader is a person who runs a small business alone, with no partners or company. The plan offered them debt forgiveness and cash.
If something is beyond the pale, it is so shocking that it falls outside acceptable behaviour. Most Brazilians decided Mr Bolsonaro's conduct qualified.
To rehash something is to go over it again, often with little new. The debates brought Mr Bolsonaro's past back into the spotlight.
Dodgy is a British informal word for suspicious, dishonest, or unreliable. It describes Mr Bolsonaro's past connections.
Militias are armed groups that are not part of the official army. In Rio they are made up of corrupt police who act as hitmen and extortionists.
A hitman is someone paid to kill another person. The article uses it for members of the militias.
Extortionists get money by threatening people. They make shopkeepers and residents pay for supposed protection.
A death squad is an armed group that carries out killings, often for a government or powerful people, outside the law.
A payroll is the list of people a person or organisation pays. Being on someone's payroll means they pay your salary.
Taxpayer money is public funds collected from citizens through taxes. Sending it to a criminal is a serious accusation.
To turn someone off means to make them lose interest or feel disgust. These ties made many women stop supporting him.
To plump for something is to choose it decisively, especially from a set of options. Silvânia had plumped for Mr Bolsonaro before changing her mind.
The final straw is the last in a series of problems that makes someone give up, from the saying about the straw that broke the camel's back.
On the eve of something means the day or evening just before it. The scandal broke just before voting day.
Lobbyists are people paid to persuade officials and politicians to act in the interest of a business or group.
Unappetising literally means not appealing to eat, and here it means unattractive. The choice between candidates was a poor one.
Baggage here means unwelcome past problems or associations that follow someone around, not suitcases.
A caucus is a group of politicians who share an aim or party and work together in a legislature.
A lame duck is an official who is about to leave office or cannot run again, and so has less power to get things done.
Creaking means old and in poor condition, like a creaking door. A creaking economy is weak and straining.
A spendthrift is a person who spends money carelessly. Lula's spendthrift policies raised the debt.
Vertigo is the dizzy feeling you get from great heights. Vertigo-inducing rates are so high they make you dizzy.
A real interest rate is the interest rate after taking away inflation, so it shows what borrowing truly costs.
A cadre is a trusted, committed member of a party or organisation. A party cadre as finance minister would be a loyalist, not an outside expert.
A heavyweight is a powerful, important person, borrowed from boxing. Markets want a respected expert.
Giveaways are free benefits handed out, often to win favour. Here they are the pre-election perks Lula promised.
Brazil's Supreme Court is the country's highest court, which handles major constitutional questions, including election disputes.
To beat the odds is to succeed even though success seemed unlikely.
